text: Pocket Minutes turns a meeting recording into minutes that never leave your device. Transcription, speaker separation, the language model, search and translation all run locally, on Tether Q V A C, on a CPU. Everything you are about to see was recorded live, inside a sandbox with no network at all.

Here is that sandbox. Only a loopback interface exists. D N S fails. A T C P connection to the internet fails. The app and the browser both run inside it, and the models were cached beforehand, so nothing here can reach a cloud.
The meeting is synthetic: three text to speech voices reading a fictional product launch sync. I press process.

The pipeline reports each stage. A fast Whisper draft appears first. Then a diarizing model works out who is speaking. Then Qwen three writes the minutes in small windows, and a verifier checks every item against the transcript. This took two and a half minutes of real compute. I have sped up the waiting, and the label says by how much.

Decisions, action items with owners, and risks. Every item cites the transcript line it came from, and suggestions the verifier could not ground were dropped. The count is shown. Click a time chip and the audio jumps to the exact second.

Ask in plain language. Embedding Gemma retrieves the relevant windows, the local model answers, and each citation is checked against what was retrieved. A question that the meeting never covered gets an honest, not discussed.
The minutes translate on device, with Bergamot, in twelve languages. About a second each.

The Offline Receipt records interfaces, failed probes, and every socket sampled during the run, attributed to the app and its worker. Zero external sockets. The entries are hash chained. I verify the chain in the browser, then tamper with one entry, and it breaks. This is evidence, not proof, and the app says so.

The benchmark is measured on this machine, on one synthetic meeting. The balanced profile found all three speakers and eleven of twelve ground truth items, at one point two times real time, and peaks near eight gigabytes of memory. The lite profile is faster and lighter, but weak: two of twelve. The numbers are published as they came out.

Real: the Q V A C pipeline, the recorded run, the receipt, the benchmark. Synthetic: the voices and the meeting. The hosted page is a replay, because Q V A C cannot run inside a web page. Pocket Minutes is open source under M I T.
